scope: Content ownership, explicit host bindings and callback semantics for proc selection. The original 143 courses remain unchanged. This is not acceptance of every proc payload or a new recovery policy.

cases.setup: Construct owned content with A then B, and one rider on A. Change the caller's arrays, row fields and nested payload afterward.
Attempt to mutate a returned definition, nested payload, ordered candidates or trigger membership.
Supply duplicate proc/rider identities, a dangling rider host, unsupported trigger, malformed filter, nonfinite number or nonportable payload.
Create two different content objects using the same proc id with different trigger/effect data.
An A effect grants a later B of the same trigger during dispatch. Only A was armed at entry.
Pulse A grants pulse B during a sweep. Only A was armed at entry; both are otherwise due.
A matching proc appends and grants B during own-event dispatch through the compatibility source.
Warm a compatibility index with A on condition. Change A to heal without changing list identity or length. Then append an unrelated row.
Two compatibility sources have equal-length lists and identical ids but different definitions.
After constructing a binding, replace callback properties and change its supplied configuration object.
An execution callback dispatches another event at depth+1, with two extra levels purchased and configured. Each random draw is zero.
At time 0, a proc with PPM 6 and ICD 2 passes its roll, then execution throws. Retry immediately, then at time 1.
A required condition read throws before the once-per-time gate.
An eligible attempt receives a nonfinite or out-of-range random sample from the host.
Dispatch two independent actors sharing immutable content and one runtime binding.
Two condition edges are queued. The first selected effect throws after the queue was detached.
